# Unequal homothetic paired tails: an exact obstruction and scalar profiles

The proposed lower bound

    r^d F(t/r)+s^d F(-t/s)
       >=min{min(r^d,s^d),2 Gamma_d((r+s)/2)^d}         (1)

is false, already for a triangle and two nearly equal scales. The failure persists when both caps are proper and have positive area.

For the two opposite facet directions of an untruncated simplex cone, Section 3 proves the exact replacement profile. Section 4 gives a complete finite formula for every centered truncated affine-power law and both orientations. These are scalar-profile theorems; no minimum over all simplex directions or all convex bodies is asserted.

Throughout, `F` is a normalized ordinary centroid tail. Actual cap volumes are the displayed quantities multiplied by the volume of the unscaled body.

## 1. Exact triangle counterexample

Start with the triangle

    T=conv{(0,0),(1,0),(1,1)},       |T|=1/2,

whose centroid is `(2/3,1/3)`. Translate it by minus that centroid to obtain `K`, and use the first-coordinate normal. Its centered marginal has density `2(x+2/3)` on `[-2/3,1/3]`, so

    F(q)=1-(q+2/3)^2      for -2/3<=q<=1/3,

with `F=1` below the support and `F=0` above it. At the upper support endpoint the closed cap is a line segment of zero area, so `F(1/3)=0` exactly.

Take

    d=2,       r=1,       s=11/10,       t=-11/30.

The large-fiber threshold is `-t/s=1/3`, and hence its cap has zero area. The small-fiber fraction is

    F(t)=1-(3/10)^2=91/100.

On the other hand the proposed right side in (1) is

    min{1,2*(4/9)*(21/20)^2}=49/50.

Thus

    91/100<49/50.                                    (2)

This is an actual homothetic geometric configuration. Place `rK` and `sK` at integer bases `-1` and `+1` and take their convex hull. Its middle fiber is `((r+s)/2)K` and its centroid is zero. The ambient halfspace

    H={ (z,x): x_1+t z>=0}

passes through that actual midpoint centroid and has precisely the two endpoint cap costs in (2). The middle fiber's contribution is not part of the proposed two-source inequality; no mixed-depth counterexample is claimed.

The supporting-facet coincidence is not essential. Replace `t` by

    t'=-109/300.

Both scalar thresholds are then strictly inside their respective supports, and both endpoint caps have positive area. Their dimensionless costs are

    F(t')=81719/90000,
    (11/10)^2 F(-t'/(11/10))=659/90000.

Their sum is `41189/45000`, still strictly below `49/50`, by the exact positive gap `2911/45000`.

## 2. An unconditional bound which does survive

Let `K` be any convex body with centroid zero and volume `V`. It contains zero in its interior. If `r<=s`, the centered homothetic copy `rK` lies in `sK`. Consequently

    s^d F(-t/s)>=r^d F(-t/r).

The proved ordinary paired-centroid-tail theorem therefore gives

    r^d F(t/r)+s^d F(-t/s)
       >=2 Gamma_d r^d.                              (3)

By interchanging the scales and replacing `t` by `-t`, the bound is `2 Gamma_d min(r^d,s^d)` in general. This observation retains a valid paired contribution, but does not claim sharp dependence on an unequal scale ratio. Its only non-elementary dependency is the already proved theorem in `candidate 732b11a769399016`, Section 1.

## 3. Exact two-orientation profile for the simplex facet marginal

For an integer `d>=1`, consider the centered probability law obtained from density `d x^(d-1)` on `[0,1]`. Put

    A=d/(d+1),       B=1/(d+1),
    F_+(q)=1-clip(A+q,0,1)^d,
    F_-(q)=1-F_+(-q).                                (4)

These are the tails in the two opposite facet directions of an actual simplex. They are continuous, so the closed-tail convention gives the displayed reflection identity even at the endpoints.

For `0<r<=s`, the exact minimum over the threshold and these **two specified orientations** is

    min_(t in R, eps in {+,-})
       [r^d F_eps(t/r)+s^d F_eps(-t/s)]
      =min{ E_d(r,s), V_d(r,s) },                     (5)

where

    E_d(r,s)=r^d-[(d r-s)_+/(d+1)]^d,
    V_d(r,s)=2 Gamma_d((r+s)/2)^d.                    (6)

The first branch is the supporting-facet cut missing from (1). The following proof treats all thresholds, not just stationary proper cuts.

### The increasing-density orientation

Write

    C(t)=r^d F_+(t/r)+s^d F_+(-t/s).

Its only clipping breakpoints are

    -rA,       rB,       -sB,       sA.                (7)

Where both caps are proper,

    C(t)=r^d+s^d-(rA+t)^d-(sA-t)^d.                 (8)

For `d>=2`, this is concave in `t`. Where exactly one cap is proper, `C` is monotone. Its two far plateaus are `r^d` and `s^d`. The minimum must therefore occur at a clipping breakpoint or plateau.

If `s<=d r`, the negative breakpoints satisfy `-rA<=-sB`. At `t=-sB` the large cap vanishes and the small cap gives `E_d(r,s)`. At the other interior junction, `t=rB`, the value is

    J_d(r,s)=s^d-[(d s-r)/(d+1)]^d.                  (9)

The remaining relevant values are at least one of these or a plateau. We have `E_d<=r^d<=s^d`, and `J_d>=E_d`. To check the latter explicitly, divide by `r^d` and put `lambda=s/r`. For `1<=lambda<=d`, the difference is

    D(lambda)=lambda^d-1
       -[(d lambda-1)^d-(d-lambda)^d]/(d+1)^d.

It vanishes at one. For `d>=2`,

    D'(lambda)/d
      =lambda^(d-1)
       -[d(d lambda-1)^(d-1)+(d-lambda)^(d-1)]/(d+1)^d
      >=lambda^(d-1)[1-(d/(d+1))^(d-1)]>0,           (10)

because both nonnegative bases in the numerator are at most `d lambda`. Hence the minimum is `E_d`.

If `s>=d r`, the small cap is still full when the large one first turns on. The relevant value at that junction is `r^d=E_d`. The value (9) is at least `r^d`: it is so at `s=d r` by (10), and increases with `s`, as follows directly by differentiation. The same monotonicity and concavity on all the intervals in (7) now give minimum `r^d=E_d`. Thus in all cases

    min_t C(t)=E_d(r,s).                             (11)

For `d=1`, the law is a centered uniform interval. Direct clipping gives minimum `r`, which agrees with (11); the derivative argument (10) is not needed.

### The opposite orientation

Continue with `d>=2`, since the interval case was handled directly. Reflection gives its cost as `r^d+s^d-C(-t)`. The only possible interior maximum of (8) is

    t_*=A(s-r)/2,

where the two positive powered terms in (8) are equal. It lies in the common proper interval exactly when

    s/r<=1+2/d.                                    (12)

When feasible its value is `r^d+s^d-V_d(r,s)`. All other possible maxima come from the far plateau `s^d`: the one-proper pieces are monotone, and if `t_*` lies to the right of the common proper interval, (8) increases up to its right endpoint, where the first cap is empty and the value is at most `s^d`. Therefore the opposite-orientation minimum is

    min{r^d,V_d(r,s)}.                               (13)

If (12) fails, `V_d(r,s)>2r^d`, so (13) still equals the correct plateau value `r^d`. Combining (11)--(13) and `E_d<=r^d` proves (5).

At equal scales, the supporting branch is no smaller than the vertex branch. Indeed

    (d+1)^d-(d-1)^d>=2d^d

by expanding the difference and retaining its first odd binomial term. Thus (5) reduces to `2 Gamma_d r^d`, agreeing with the audited equal-scale paired-tail theorem. For `d=2`, the exact formula is

    min{r^2-[(2r-s)_+/3]^2, 2((r+s)/3)^2}.

This is the exact minimum for the two opposite facet normals; it is not asserted to describe every simplex direction.

## 4. Complete finite profile for every truncated affine-power law

Fix `d>=1` and `0<=a<1`. Let `X` have density

    d x^(d-1)/(1-a^d),       a<=x<=1,

and mean

    m=d/(d+1)*(1-a^(d+1))/(1-a^d).

Its centered tail is

    F_a(q)=[1-clip(m+q,a,1)^d]/(1-a^d).              (14)

These laws are realized by the first-coordinate marginals of actual convex frusta with sections homothetic to `x L`, where `L` is any full-dimensional convex body in `R^(d-1)` containing zero; `d=1` is simply an interval. Translating the full frustum by its centroid centers the marginal.

For arbitrary positive scales `r,s`, put

    C_a(t)=r^d F_a(t/r)+s^d F_a(-t/s),
    W=r^d+s^d,

and form the finite set of scalar values

    E={r^d,s^d}
       union {C_a(t):t in B_a},                      (15)

where

    B_a={r(a-m), r(1-m), s(m-1), s(m-a),
                                      m(s-r)/2}.    (16)

Then the exact minimum over all thresholds and both reflected orientations is

    min{ min E, W-max E }.                           (17)

Formula (17) includes all empty/full endpoint cases and does not require the stationary candidate in (16) to be a proper cut.

To prove it, split the real line at the first four thresholds in (16). On every resulting interval, a cap is either constant or proper. With one proper cap the cost is monotone; with neither it is constant. With both proper, differentiation gives

    C_a'(t)=d/(1-a^d)
       [(s m-t)^(d-1)-(r m+t)^(d-1)].                (18)

For `d>=2` this has at most one zero, at the fifth candidate in (16), and the second derivative is nonpositive. For `d=1` the expression is zero throughout the common proper interval, whose endpoints are already in the list. Thus both extrema are attained among the endpoint values, any feasible stationary value, and the two far plateaus. Including the stationary evaluation even when it is outside the proper interval cannot alter the extrema: it is still an actual value of the same function, while all true extremal values are already present. Hence `min C_a=min E` and `max C_a=max E`. The reflected orientation costs `W-C_a(-t)`, proving (17).

For rational `a,r,s`, every entry of (15) is rational. Formula (17) is therefore an exact finite arithmetic profile for each localized affine-power law. It does not by itself optimize over `a`, nor does this note invoke a localization theorem to assert a new sharp bound for every convex body.

The verifier `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_unequal_homothetic_paired_profiles.py` checks the triangle cap fractions, the proper-cut perturbation, and exact finite-profile/closed-form agreement on rational calibrations. The general interval decomposition and inequalities above are the proofs; no finite screen is used as a universal argument.
